title: Present-Tense Mood — First Look (أَنْ / لَنْ / لَمْ)

steps.title: A verb has its own case system — mood
body: Nouns mark their role with case (رَفْع/نَصْب/جَرّ — gr:case-system). The present-tense VERB marks something different — mood — using two of the same three Arabic names, plus a third: مَرْفُوع, مَنْصُوب, مَجْزُوم. Same names, completely different system: this marks the verb's own ending, not a noun's role.
مَرْفُوع is the default — the plain present tense you already know, ending in ḍamma ـُ: هُوَ يَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ ("he goes to school"). Nothing before the verb triggers anything else.
أَنْ ("to") and لَنْ ("will never") both trigger مَنْصُوب — replace the ḍamma with fatḥa ـَ: هُوَ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ... ("he wants to go..."), هُوَ لَنْ يَذْهَبَ... ("he will never go...").

لَمْ ("did not") triggers مَجْزُوم — drop the ending vowel entirely (sukūn, no vowel at all): هُوَ لَمْ يَذْهَبْ... ("he did not go..."). This is the first way you've seen to negate a PAST-tense verbal sentence — gr:negation-a1's لَيْسَ/لَا/مَا only negate a nominal sentence.

steps.title: Four sentences, one verb, three moods
steps.intro: Read all four and compare the ending on يَذْهَبُ/يَذْهَبَ/يَذْهَبْ each time. Tap 🔊 to hear any line.

steps.title: The default mood
steps.prompt: No mood-triggering particle appears here. What mood is يَذْهَبُ?

options.label: مَرْفُوع — the default, since nothing before it triggers a different mood
مَنْصُوب — every present-tense verb needs a mood particle
مَجْزُوم — sukūn is the default ending for verbs

steps.explanation: مَرْفُوع is the default mood. A present-tense verb only becomes مَنْصُوب or مَجْزُوم when a specific trigger particle (أَنْ, لَنْ, لَمْ, and others not yet taught) sits directly before it.

steps.title: أَنْ triggers مَنْصُوب
steps.arabicPrompt: هُوَ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ
steps.prompt: يَذْهَبَ ends in fatḥa here, not the usual ḍamma. Why?

options.label: أَنْ triggers مَنْصُوب on the verb right after it
All present-tense verbs end in fatḥa
يَذْهَبَ is the subject of the sentence

steps.explanation: أَنْ is a subjunctive particle — a present-tense verb right after it takes مَنْصُوب, replacing the default ḍamma with fatḥa.

steps.title: لَنْ also triggers مَنْصُوب
steps.prompt: What mood is يَذْهَبَ in here, and why?

options.label: مَنْصُوب — لَنْ triggers it, just like أَنْ

steps.explanation: لَنْ negates the future and, like أَنْ, pushes the verb after it into مَنْصُوب — fatḥa instead of ḍamma.

steps.title: لَمْ triggers مَجْزُوم — and negates the past
steps.prompt: يَذْهَبْ has no ending vowel at all here. What mood is that, and what does the sentence mean?

options.label: مَجْزُوم, triggered by لَمْ — "he did NOT go to school" (past, despite the present-tense verb shape)
مَجْزُوم, triggered by لَمْ — "he does not go to school" (present)
مَنْصُوب, triggered by لَمْ — the same mood as أَنْ/لَنْ

steps.explanation: لَمْ triggers its own mood, مَجْزُوم — sukūn, no vowel at all, distinct from مَنْصُوب's fatḥa. لَمْ specifically negates the PAST, even though the verb after it keeps its present-tense shape.

steps.title: A verb's own case system
steps.message: مَرْفُوع (default) / مَنْصُوب (أَنْ, لَنْ) / مَجْزُوم (لَمْ) — three moods on the present-tense verb, and a real new way to negate the past. كَيْ, حَتَّى, لِـ, لَا النَّاهِيَة, لَام الْأَمْر, and the conditional particles are still ahead, along with how plural/dual forms mark مَجْزُوم.
